entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Akhilesh Kumar Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.248 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 306 IPC,
Police Station Haidarganj, District Faizabad/ Ayodhya.
3.

In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant 8 years ago and subsequently, they were lot of disputes in between them and the applicant used to hit the daughter of the informant and subsequently on account of being harassed mentally and physically she committed suicide on 26.12.2023.
Rajendra Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Rajendra Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. The Counsel for the applicant argues that there is no material to suggest the abetment at the instance of the applicant as defined under Section 107 of IPC.
5.

Learned A.G.A. oppose the bail prayer by arguing that the suicide was committed on being harassed by the applicant.
6. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

7. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, from the documents, there is no material to suggest or establish abetment at the instance of the applicant as defined under Section 107 of IPC and in view of the law as explained in the case of Mariano Anto Bruno and another vs Inspector of Police; 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1387 coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 01.01.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

entities.text: Mariano Anto Bruno and another vs Inspector of Police; 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1387
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Rajendra Mishra be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 12.3.2024 akverma  Rajendra Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
